gacc_sections.narrative: * Round Prarie, Louisiana Office of Forestry. Eight miles northwest of Bastrop, LA. Southern rough. Active fire behavior with wind-driven runs and short crown runs. Hydra, Texas A&M Forest Service. Three miles south of Meridian, TX. Brush and grass. Minimal fire behavior with smoldering. Gracemont, Anadarko Agency, BIA. Six miles east of Binger, OK. Timber. Moderate fire behavior with creeping and smoldering. Bunker, Arkansas Forestry Commission. Two miles east of East Camden, AR. Southern rough and timber. Minimal fire behavior with flanking and backing. Last report unless significant activity occurs.

Dome, Yosemite National Park, NPS. CIMT (CA Team 3). One mile north of Wawona, CA. Timber, brush and heavy slash. Moderate fire behavior with flanking, uphill runs and single tree torching. Area, road and trail closures in effect. Plaskett, Los Padres NF, USFS. CIMT (CA Team 6). CIMT is also managing the Timber incident. Thirty-four miles southwest of Big Sur, CA. Chaparral, grass and timber. Minimal fire behavior with creeping and backing. Area and trail closures in effect. Timber, Los Padres NF, USFS. Four miles southeast of Big Sur, CA. Grass, timber and chaparral. Minimal fire behavior with creeping and backing. Numerous structures and communication infrastructure threatened. Area, road and trail closures in effect.

Chileno, Marin County Fire Department. Nine miles east of Tomales, CA. Grass. Minimal fire behavior. Structures threatened. Area closures in effect. Floriston, Nevada-Yuba-Placer Unit, Cal Fire. predictive_services_discussion: The lower Mississippi Valley will be the main area of concern today as warm temperatures and dry relative humidities re-establish after isolated thunderstorms moved over the area yesterday. Relative humidity will fall to 35-40% as temperatures rise back into the low to mid 90s, and there will be a few isolated thunderstorms today as well. The reorientation of the high pressure ridge over the southeast will allow southerly flow to draw another round of monsoonal moisture into New Mexico and eastern Arizona, and 2-5 inches of rain is expected there today. Breezy west winds will develop through Cascade gaps this afternoon with gusts to 35 mph, slightly stronger than yesterday. This will include the Columbia Gorge. Relative humidity will drop to 10-20% across northern California with breezy winds and poor overnight humidity recovery again today, though significant fire potential will remain low. A weak cold front moving south through the southern plains will continue to bring isolated showers and thunderstorms to parts of Texas and western Oklahoma.
